brief.title: Test repeat purchase before selecting a format.
brief.summary: Keep comparing paid repeat and contribution across existing shelf-stable, fresh and functional options. A newly recorded Fi supplement recall adds a supplier-control check before consumer trials. Fancy Feast's Amazon-exclusive collection adds channel context, not evidence of demand.
brief.question: Which option offers a clear advantage at a price owners will keep paying?

assumptions.title: Fresh and mixed feeding can expand beyond a premium niche.
assumptions.question: Is growth incremental to the category, or mainly switching from existing products?

assumptions.title: Consumers will pay more for benefits they can understand and verify.
assumptions.question: Which benefits sustain repeat purchase at the target price?

assumptions.title: Retail access and convenience can be as important as the proposition.
assumptions.question: Which channel or distribution constraint could prevent adoption?

signals.title: Fi supplement recall adds a supplier-control check
signals.source: Fi / Vet Plus, Inc.; announcement hosted by FDA
signals.fact: Fi announced a recall on September 3; FDA published it September 8. It covers 180 g Calming supplements lot 26118 and 180 g 8-in-1 Formula supplements lot 26159 for possible Salmonella linked to a supplied ingredient. Fi reported its manufacturer suspended production during investigation. Distribution included direct sales, Amazon and Chewy.
signals.implication: Include ingredient qualification and lot traceability in prototype safety checks; benefit substantiation alone does not address manufacturing risk.
signals.question: Can a proposed supplier document ingredient controls, batch release and traceability before any feeding trial?
signals.origin: Company announcement September 3; FDA publication September 8; newly recorded September 11, 2026
signals.limitation: Company recall notice, not a completed root-cause investigation. These two supplement lots do not establish risk rates for other supplements, dental chews or fresh food, or a change in willingness to pay.

signals.title: Fancy Feast uses an Amazon-exclusive curated collection
signals.fact: Fancy Feast announced The Paige Edit on September 10. The release dates initial Amazon-exclusive availability to September 1, while supplies last. The collection includes two Gems recipes and one Classic Broths recipe; the company distinguishes complete adult-cat Gems meals from supplemental Broths.
signals.implication: A curated bundle of existing recipes is another route to test discovery and channel fit without assuming a new formulation is needed.
signals.question: Would a curated bundle produce paid repeat beyond promotion, compared with buying the same recipes separately?
signals.limitation: Company-reported availability, not independently checked stock, sales, retention or incremental demand. A limited collection does not prove channel exclusivity improves adoption.

signals.title: Owners combine premium intentions with value choices
signals.fact: APPA's 2026 Dog Report, based on its 2025 National Pet Owners Survey, reported premium food fed by 31% of owners and basic food by 21%. It reported 32% buying dog food at supermarkets and 22% at discount retailers, alongside greater blending of premium and budget choices.
signals.implication: An affordable premium add-on may fit current routines better than an exclusively premium feeding proposition.
signals.question: Which owner segments protect premium benefits, and what per-meal price threshold drives switching or blending?
signals.limitation: Trade-association survey summary; historical 2025 behavior, not a live measure of September 2026 shopping.

signals.title: Blue Buffalo launches fresh food through major retailers
signals.fact: Blue Buffalo announced the nationwide launch of Love Made Fresh in resealable tubs and slice-and-serve rolls. The announcement named Walmart, Target, Kroger and Meijer among retailers and explicitly positioned the range for mixing fresh food with dry food.
signals.implication: A flexible fresh topper may offer a more accessible upgrade than asking owners to replace their entire feeding routine.
signals.question: Which pack size, daily serving cost and storage format best support repeat purchase among mixed-feeding households?
signals.limitation: Company announcement; establishes launch and positioning, not market adoption or sales performance.

signals.title: Football rituals become pet-treat occasions
signals.fact: Blue Buffalo announced Game Day Nudges in football-themed packaging and football-shaped Health Bars Touchdown Treats. The company reported Game Day Nudges available at participating retailers and scheduled Health Bars Touchdown Treats for November 2.
signals.implication: Limited seasonal shapes and packaging could create incremental treating occasions tied to shared household rituals.
signals.question: Do these occasions add category purchases or mainly shift purchases from the everyday treat range?
signals.limitation: Company announcement. November 2 availability is a future launch plan as of verification, not a completed rollout.

signals.title: One cat-food format offers two meal experiences
signals.fact: Blue Buffalo introduced a cat food that can be served dry or mixed with water to create gravy. The launch offered chicken-and-brown-rice and salmon-and-brown-rice recipes and reported availability at major retailers nationwide.
signals.implication: Shelf-stable meal customization could offer owners more serving variety without adding another food format to the pantry.
signals.question: Does the two-mode format improve repeat purchase, perceived variety or ease of serving in multicat households?
signals.limitation: Company announcement; functional benefits and category-first language are manufacturer claims, not independently validated here.

signals.title: Fresh format expands into veterinary diets
signals.fact: Royal Canin announced its first fresh, fully cooked therapeutic diet portfolio for dogs in the United States. The range covers gastrointestinal low-fat, selected-protein pork and appetite-stimulation formulas, distributed through veterinary practices and veterinary online pharmacy partners.
signals.implication: Fresh food may increasingly compete on clinical credibility and professional distribution, alongside ingredient and lifestyle positioning.
signals.question: What clinical evidence, channel partnerships and cold-chain capabilities would be required to compete credibly?
signals.limitation: Manufacturer launch announcement; the formulas' therapeutic positioning is reported, not independently assessed.

signals.title: Purina adds capacity and manufacturing flexibility
signals.fact: Purina announced the opening of a Batavia, Ohio factory representing an investment exceeding $550 million. The company said the factory was already producing Pro Plan, Purina ONE and Dog Chow, and incorporated automation, robotics and digital manufacturing tools.
signals.implication: Large investments in flexible capacity may increase competitive pressure on availability, operating efficiency and product iteration.
signals.question: Which formats and channels gain capacity, and does this change competitive service levels or launch cadence?
signals.limitation: Company announcement; capacity and operating benefits are reported plans and claims rather than independently audited outcomes.

signals.title: A raw-food recall raises a process-control question
signals.fact: An FDA-hosted company announcement recalled two specified frozen raw chicken pet-food lots following positive contamination tests. The announcement reported nationwide retail distribution and no illnesses reported at the time of the announcement.
signals.implication: Process transparency and demonstrated safety controls could influence trust in less-processed food propositions.
signals.question: How do owners distinguish raw from fully cooked fresh food, and which safety information changes purchase confidence?
signals.limitation: FDA-hosted company recall notice; a lot-specific incident, not evidence that all fresh foods share the same risk.

signals.title: Pet ownership grows while spending becomes more selective
signals.fact: APPA reported total U.S. pet-industry expenditure of $158 billion in 2025 and forecast $165 billion for 2026. The report put 2025 pet ownership at 95 million U.S. households and cat ownership at 53 million households, up 5% year over year.
signals.implication: Cat-focused innovation could merit greater attention, but category expenditure growth alone does not establish demand for a specific food concept.
signals.question: Which cat-food needs and formats show incremental demand after separating household growth, price and consumption?
signals.limitation: Total pet-industry figures include categories beyond food; 2026 expenditure is a forecast, not an actual result.

runs.summary: Morning research pass: reviewed 11 distinct readable public pages: 10 primary pages (FDA recall index, Fi notice, Northwest Naturals notice; APPA news index; Purina news index, Paige Edit and Innovation Prize announcements; General Mills football-treat announcement; Chewy corporate overview; Freshpet Q2 results) and one Houston Chronicle lead used only to locate the FDA notice. Search snippets, repeat opens, failed pages and empty indexes are excluded. Added two URL/event-deduplicated signals: Fi's September 3 recall, posted by FDA September 8, and Fancy Feast's September 10 announcement of September 1 availability. Rechecked existing raw-recall, football-launch and Freshpet evidence without duplicating events. Fi contextualizes value/benefit validation; the bundle contextualizes access. Neither resolves willingness to pay, incremental format growth or the importance of distribution. Opportunity rankings and proposed experiments remain unchanged. Updated both evidence files; preserved prior records and history. Workspace records returned zero rows, so there were no queued missions, scenarios or user overrides to apply. Coverage gaps: Chewy release content was unavailable, Freshpet's news index failed, and Tetra Pak's case index did not load usable article content. No new consumer survey, retail sell-through, entrant cost quotes, technology outcome or global regulatory change was verified. Purina's September 1 prize announcement was reviewed but not added as evidence of demand or proven technology. This was a bounded public-source scan, not exhaustive market coverage.
Ran opportunity and adversarial research tracks. Revised novelty and fresh-affordability assumptions, then designed comparative experiments. Commercial scenarios remain explicitly illustrative.

Established an eight-source baseline across launches, consumer value choices, veterinary distribution, manufacturing and safety. Separated historical survey results and future plans from observed events.
